label: Start here
title: Your token, in a multicurrency framework
intro: IMF brings project collateral, currency positions and liquidity planning into one workflow.
html:
What IMF is for

The International Multicurrency Framework (IMF) is an independent extension of Frankencoin mechanics for projects that want to use tokens as collateral and mint a selected currency token on DogeOS. Project treasuries are the primary users. Other participants can assess proposals, provide equity, use savings, challenge positions or bid in auctions under the same contracts.

One currency at a time

Every position belongs to one of 11 currency systems. Each system has its own currency token, minting hub, equity and pool shares, savings/leadrate, positions and source bridge. There is no automatic FX conversion, shared reserve, shared basket or cross-currency exposure engine. A project working in two currencies has two independent risk and repayment workflows.

Three places to work

  • Website: understand the framework and choose a next step.
  • Documentation: learn exact position, bridge, equity and savings mechanics.
  • App: inspect configured reads and prepare a human or agent position plan.
Current integration boundary: no live V2 deployment registry is configured. This release does not claim a live V2 read connection, current on-chain rates, production availability or audit coverage. The SDK and MCP integration is read-only: no signing, transaction simulation, DEX execution or challenger infrastructure is included. Drafts stay in browser storage for the app origin and are not cloud-synchronized.

Begin with your project

Identify the collateral contract and decimals, the treasury that will own the position, and the currency you intend to repay. Choose a new proposal, accepted-term clone or existing-position mint. Prepare the collateral and any opening fee, then budget a separate project-token allocation if you also want DEX liquidity.

Plan a position

IMF is independent of the International Monetary Fund and is not an official Frankencoin or DogeOS product. No affiliation, endorsement or partnership is implied.

label: Project workflow
title: From token treasury to currency liquidity
intro: A practical sequence for project teams, with human and agent responsibilities.
html:
1. Choose the operation, not just the collateral

  • New proposal: configure all position terms, fund the irrevocable 1,000-local-unit opening fee and observe an initialization period of at least three days.
  • Clone accepted terms: reuse a valid parent and its family terms without the opening fee. The caller funds collateral, while the child owner and child expiration are explicit inputs.
  • Mint an existing position: do not create a position or pay another opening fee. Check caller rights, state, family capacity, backing and the current upfront fee.

These paths are not interchangeable. See proposal terms and borrowing quotes.

2. Prepare method-specific inputs

Record the currency instance and contract addresses, position owner, collateral funder and recipient. Keep collateral in its own raw decimals, local currency and fees in 18-decimal local raw units, rates in parts per million (ppm), and timestamps in seconds. A liquidation price has 36 − collateralDecimals decimals.

For a new proposal, the treasury needs the initial collateral, the hub allowance for that collateral and 1,000 local currency units for the opening fee. For a clone, the caller—not an assumed parent owner—must supply the initial collateral. An existing mint uses collateral already held by the position.

3. Read eligibility at an identified block

Confirm chain and contract identity before reading terms. For minting, check challengedAmount == 0, closed == false, now > cooldown, now < expiration, owner-or-roller caller rights, available family capacity and collateral backing. availableForMinting() alone does not establish eligibility.

Every quote or state view needs a block number and timestamp. Loading, failed, unknown and stale reads remain unavailable—not zero, false or eligible. The public imf.li release includes the DogeOS Chikyū USD V2 testnet registry; tUSDC is a test asset. Illustrative drafts are not live position state. Other builds may be unconfigured or synthetic, so always check the current registry and source-block reads.

4. Keep DEX liquidity separate

After minting, any DEX plan uses currency in the wallet plus additional project tokens that were never locked as collateral. Verify the DEX, pair, token addresses, price, fee tier, range, minimum outputs and LP controller separately. This frontend does not execute DEX transactions or certify a pool. It also does not introduce a circular-liquidity policy; participants must assess the liquidity and collateral relationship themselves.

5. Manage debt and time independently

Track gross debt, wallet repayment amount, currently assigned reserve, collateral, cooldown, challenges and expiration. Repayment can remain possible when withdrawal is blocked. Debt-free does not mean closed, and rolling a position is not automatic. Use the repayment and withdrawal guide and maturity and rolling guide.

Human and agent views use the same read and plan inputs. Exported JSON is a planning document only. Simulation and signer authorization are separate operations outside this read-only integration; private keys never belong in a draft.

label: Collateral proposals
title: Make the proposal understandable
intro: The interface supports participant decisions; it does not approve projects.
html:
New proposal: terms and hard bounds

A new openPosition call configures the collateral, minimum and initial collateral, family minting maximum, initialization, duration, challenge period, risk premium, liquidation price and reserve contribution. The opening fee is 1,000 units of the selected local currency, represented as 1000 × 1e18 raw units, and is irrevocable. The initialization input must be at least 3 days.

  • Initial collateral must be at least the minimum collateral.
  • riskPremiumPPM ≤ 1,000,000.
  • 20,000 ≤ reserveContributionPPM ≤ 1,000,000: the minimum is 2%, not 20%.
  • Collateral decimals must be at most 24, and the token must revert on a failed transfer to be compatible with the hub's check.
  • minimumCollateral × price ≥ 3500e36.
  • minimumCollateral × price ≤ mintingMaximum × 1e18.

The two products above use raw integer inputs. mintingMaximum is an 18-decimal local amount. price has 36 − collateralDecimals decimals: 18 decimals for an 18-decimal token, 30 for a 6-decimal token and 36 for a 0-decimal token. Do not format a price with local-currency decimals.

Clone accepted terms: same family, explicit child expiry

Cloning does not charge the new-position opening fee. The parent must belong to the selected hub and be cloneable: no open challenge, not closed, now > cooldown and now < expiration. The initial collateral must meet the inherited minimum. The caller funds that collateral; the requested child owner receives the initial mint and subsequent ownership.

The child belongs to the original position's family and shares its minting capacity. Its price is copied from the parent, while its expiration is an absolute timestamp no later than the original expiration. The initializer rejects a past timestamp; because cloning always attempts the initial mint, a successful clone also needs now < childExpiration. Quote the fee with parent.calculateFee(childExpiration), not parent.calculateCurrentFee(), which uses the parent's expiration.

Existing mint: no proposal shortcut

An existing-position mint still requires the owner or recognized roller, no challenge, not closed, now > cooldown, now < expiration, family capacity and sufficient collateral backing. For an original, capacity starts with the family limit less total family minted. Clone availability also accounts for the original's unused collateral-backed potential through availableForClones(). Reserve plus the calculated fee must not exceed 1,000,000 ppm.

Assessment remains a participant responsibility

Qualified participants can veto a new position only while now < start. At start, denial is too late; because initial cooldown == start, minting still requires a later timestamp with now > cooldown. Displaying a token or DEX pair does not certify collateral quality, liquidity, legality or safety.

Status must come from verified contracts

Distinguish a local draft, submitted proposal, review window, vetoed/closed position and read-eligible position. None is established by a JSON export. A connected interface must identify the registry, chain, contract versions and read block; this release has no configured live V2 registry from which to display those states.

label: Mechanism
title: Frankencoin mechanics, currency by currency
intro: Collateralized positions, retained reserves, public challenges and equity.
html:
An independent extension

IMF extends Frankencoin-style collateralized minting, challenges, savings and pool-share governance into independently parameterized currency systems. It is not an official Frankencoin deployment. References to upstream documentation explain lineage only; they do not establish affiliation or extend upstream audit coverage to IMF V2, its deployment or its source assets.

Gross debt and usable proceeds

A position records minted, the gross 18-decimal local-currency debt including the reserve component. Minting allocates gross amount between usable wallet currency, the position's assigned minter reserve and an upfront fee. The fee depends on the current leadrate plus the position risk premium and time to expiration. It is not a universal 20% reserve or 1% fee model. See the exact borrowing arithmetic.

Capacity and backing are different checks

Family capacity limits how much more gross currency a position family can mint. Collateral backing checks that relevantCollateral × price ≥ minted × 1e18. Below the minimum collateral, relevant collateral is treated as zero. A position can have capacity but fail backing, or have backing but be blocked by a challenge, closure, cooldown or expiration.

Oracle-free does not mean unattended

No external spot-price oracle automatically liquidates a position. Participants can challenge the stored price before expiration, avert during the first phase or bid in the later Dutch auction. Expired collateral follows a different forced-sale curve. The interface supplies no challenger or keeper service; monitoring and action remain participant responsibilities. Read the boundary-by-boundary challenge guide.

Reserve, equity and savings are distinct

The minter reserve is assigned to position issuance; equity belongs to pool-share holders after subtracting tracked minter reserve from the reserve token balance. Severe losses can impair minter reserve and change repayment arithmetic. Savings uses the per-currency leadrate and pays accrued interest only up to available equity. Pool shares, currency tokens and DEX LP tokens are different assets.

Independent currency systems

Each currency has separate token supply, pool shares, reserves, positions, savings, losses and bridge accounting. There is no shared reserve, automatic FX conversion or cross-currency exposure cap. A project in two currencies must manage two debts and two repayment assets.

Reference material

Read the Frankencoin position documentation and risk documentation for behavioral background. IMF's selected V2 contracts and verified deployment state determine its actual execution terms.

label: Currencies
title: Eleven units. Separate systems.
intro: Choose a denomination deliberately; every position owes its own currency.
html:
CurrencyPlanning token identifierReference unit
USDK9USDUS dollar
EURK9EUREuro
JPYK9JPYJapanese yen
GBPK9GBPPound sterling
AUDK9AUDAustralian dollar
CNYK9CNYChinese yuan
BRLK9BRLBrazilian real
PKRK9PKRPakistani rupee
BDTK9BDTBangladeshi taka
INRK9INRIndian rupee
NGNK9NGNNigerian naira

Identifiers come from V2 configuration, not a live registry. No current deployment addresses or currency availability are asserted here.

Choosing a currency

Consider the unit needed for operations, the intended DEX pair and the asset in which you can repay. A position opened in one currency records and repays debt only in that currency token. The framework does not convert debt or proceeds into another code.

Nominal units are not FX rates

A source bridge can lock a source token and mint an equal nominal number of local units after decimal normalization. That arithmetic is not a market FX conversion and does not make 100 source units worth 100 units of every currency. The test bootstrap uses valueless test tokens and is not fiat backing. See source bridges and credits.

Reference value and market value

The reference currency is a design denomination, not a promise of fiat redemption or a fixed market price. Secondary-market prices and liquidity can diverge. Position collateral and participant auction behavior also do not create a protocol FX peg.

No hidden cross-currency exposure

Projects using the same currency share that system's reserve economics. Separate currencies do not. There is no combined project exposure limit, cross-currency collateral set or shared loss pool in V2. Cross-currency project exposure remains outside this integration.

Availability and rates

All 11 codes are available for offline planning. That does not assert deployment, mintability, liquidity or a current leadrate. Initial leadrate configuration is a dated deployment input, not a live observation or return promise; consult the savings and rate-clock guide.

label: DEX liquidity
title: Take the position plan to a DEX
intro: Minting currency and providing liquidity are separate actions.
html:
Prepare two separate allocations

Your deposited collateral stays in the collateral position. To provide liquidity, budget another allocation of project tokens alongside usable minted currency or other currency already in the wallet. Record both allocations, their owners and their approvals in the treasury plan. Gross debt, usable proceeds and DEX inventory are not interchangeable balances.

Plan a pair on Barkswap

  1. Independently verify the selected network, DEX contracts and both token addresses.
  2. Choose the project-token/currency pair and inspect pool price and available liquidity.
  3. For concentrated liquidity, select the fee tier and price range and understand the resulting position.
  4. Review each token approval, input amount, minimum output and deadline in a separate transaction tool.
  5. Record the LP position, its controlling wallet and the process for later adjustment or removal.

Mentioning Barkswap describes an intended workflow, not an endorsement, partnership or assertion that a suitable pool exists.

No circular-liquidity policy is added here

This scope does not create a new circular-liquidity rule or a frontend liquidity approval gate. Projects, vetoes and other participants must assess the economic relationship between the collateral token, minted currency and pool for themselves. A pool containing related tokens is not independent proof of collateral value, exit liquidity or reserves.

Manage the two positions independently

Removing DEX liquidity does not repay currency debt. Repaying debt does not close or withdraw the LP position. Collateral withdrawal and LP withdrawal have different owners, assets, restrictions and risks. Keep both in treasury reporting without double-counting their tokens.

This read-only integration does not create pools, sign approvals, simulate swaps or execute liquidity transactions. An exported position plan is not DEX calldata or spending authority.

label: Agent workflows
title: The same intent, in structured form
intro: Prepare with an agent. Review with your treasury. Authorize through a separate signer.
html:
Equivalent human and agent inputs

Both workflows must use the same currency identity, chain ID, registry evidence, contract addresses, caller, recipient, raw amounts, decimals and timestamps. They share exact integer arithmetic and read models. Caller-dependent checks, including owner-or-roller eligibility, require an identified caller; a missing caller makes that result unknown rather than eligible.

The available operating sequence

  1. Configure: supply a verified V2 registry and suitable read endpoint. No such live registry is configured in this release.
  2. Verify identity: check generation, network, chain ID, bytecode and cross-contract links before treating registry state as verified.
  3. Read: obtain position, reserve, bridge, savings, equity or governance state with block number and timestamp.
  4. Prepare: construct a specific proposal, clone, mint, repayment or management plan using exact raw units.
  5. Review locally: export or save the intent, including assumptions and unavailable checks.

Simulation, signing, broadcasting and reconciliation are deliberately outside this integration. Do not describe a read-derived quote as a successful simulation or an exported plan as an executed MCP request.

Quotes carry assumptions

A pre-opening quote uses the current leadrate read plus proposed risk premium, reserve and assumed start/expiration timestamps. A custom-expiration clone must use the child expiration. Full-repayment and custom-expiration roll candidates require transaction simulation before execution; this integration does not perform that simulation. See borrowing costs, repayment and rolling limitations.

Read health is part of the result

Preserve the source block, observation time and freshness policy with every answer. Loading, failed, unknown, stale, wrong-chain and missing-code states are not zero balances, zero rates, no challenge or available capacity. Agents must return those states explicitly instead of filling gaps with plausible values.

Local data and permissions

Drafts remain in storage local to the app origin. Another origin does not share them, and there is no cloud synchronization. Exported JSON can be reviewed or transported by the user, but grants no on-chain authority. Never put private keys, seed phrases or signer secrets in the interface, plan, registry or agent prompt.

label: Participation & status
title: Know the action. Know the responsibility.
intro: Clear ownership of decisions, without an implied frontend approval process.
html:
Project teams

Choose the collateral, currency, owner and terms; provide the opening fee and collateral where applicable; review exact transactions; and manage repayment, withdrawal, maturity and any separate DEX position. Keep a reserve of the actual currency owed if repayment is intended. A project's market narrative is not a contract read.

Governance and market participants

Pool-share holders assess collateral and proposals, maintain any delegations and exercise qualified veto or rate rights. Challengers and bidders supply their own monitoring, capital and transactions. Qualified governance requires strictly more than 2% of time-weighted votes; it is not a frontend badge. See governance and clocks.

No keeper or challenger service is provided

The read-only interface does not watch positions for you, submit challenges, avert auctions, buy expired collateral, apply pending rates or roll maturing debt. Participants are responsible for those actions and their timing. A displayed deadline is not a promise that an agent will act.

Interface responsibilities

Present terms, units and state accurately; identify the read block; distinguish illustrative inputs from contract reads and local drafts from confirmed positions. Failed, unknown and stale reads must remain visible as such. The interface must not turn missing data into zero or enable an action from availableForMinting() alone.

Current release

No live V2 registry is configured. The integration supports read/plan workflows only and includes no signing, transaction simulation, DEX execution or production publication. Local drafts are origin-local and have no cloud sync. No current rates, live deployment, production launch or verified operational status is claimed.

Independent identity and review scope

IMF means International Multicurrency Framework. It is independent of the International Monetary Fund and is not an official Frankencoin or DogeOS product. Barkswap references describe a possible workflow, not a partnership. IMF V2 does not inherit upstream audit coverage, and no audit, MiCA compliance or decentralization certification is asserted. Production source-asset trust also remains unresolved.

label: Collateral & debt
title: More collateral than debt. Different from more cash.
intro: See collateral value, gross currency debt and wallet proceeds as three separate quantities.
html:
What overcollateralization describes

It compares collateral value with gross debt expressed in the same currency unit. In the example, assumed collateral value is twice gross minted debt. That does not mean the treasury receives 50,000 spendable units: reserve and upfront fee reduce usable proceeds, while the opening fee and external transaction costs are separate.

Token quantity is not token value

One million tokens does not imply a particular value. The contract's stored liquidation price is a position parameter used for backing and challenges, not an external market valuation. Participants still need to assess the asset, liquidity and whether that stored price is reasonable.

The contract backing inequality

For raw collateral and local amounts, the invariant is relevantCollateral × price ≥ minted × 1e18. price has 36 − collateralDecimals decimals. If collateral is below minimumCollateral, relevant collateral is zero; with positive debt, that cannot satisfy the invariant. This backing check is separate from family capacity and minting eligibility.

For live-term arithmetic, use the V2 borrowing-cost guide, not this learning bar.

What changes over time?

The leadrate, fee time horizon, collateral balance, debt, challenges and reserve coverage can change. Market conditions can change independently of the stored price. Overcollateralization does not prevent loss, currency price divergence or a failed read, and the oracle-free mechanism depends on participants acting.

Next: how can a stored price be contested?

label: Oracle-free challenges
title: Follow a price disagreement into the arena.
intro: Oracle-free replaces an external liquidation price feed with participant challenges and auctions.
html:
Starting a challenge

A challenger commits the position's collateral token and supplies a minimum-price guard against an adverse price change. New challenges require now < expiration; none can start at or after expiration. The challenged size must be nonzero and generally at least the position minimum, unless it covers the entire remaining collateral balance.

A challenge is an economic action, not a free price report. The challenger may disagree with the stored liquidation price, but the subsequent transfer, bid and settlement rules determine the result.

Exact aversion and auction boundaries

  • now == challenge.start: bid selects the aversion branch, but same-transaction aversion is explicitly rejected. This timestamp is not a successful auction bid path.
  • challenge.start < now ≤ challenge.start + challengePeriod: a bid averts all or part of the challenge. A non-challenger pays the corresponding collateral size × stored liquidation price to the challenger and receives that collateral. The challenger can cancel its own challenge without paying itself. Aversion imposes a one-day minting cooldown on the position.
  • now > challenge.start + challengePeriod: the bid follows the Dutch-auction path, returns the challenged collateral to the challenger and sells collateral to the bidder under the auction settlement rules.
  • now ≥ challenge.start + 2 × challengePeriod: the auction price is zero. Before that, the integer contract curve declines from the stored price after the aversion boundary toward zero.

At exactly challenge.start + challengePeriod, a bid still averts; the auction requires a strictly later timestamp. Existing challenges can continue after position expiration, but no new challenge can begin there.

Expired collateral uses another curve

expiredPurchasePrice is not the ordinary Dutch-auction price. For an expired position with no open challenge, forced sale uses these exact anchors:

  • now ≤ expiration: 10× liquidation price, including exactly at expiration; the position's forced-sale method itself requires expiration to have been reached.
  • expiration < now ≤ expiration + challengePeriod: declines from 10× to 1×, reaching exactly 1× at the first boundary.
  • expiration + challengePeriod < now < expiration + 2 × challengePeriod: declines from 1× toward zero.
  • now ≥ expiration + 2 × challengePeriod: zero.

Forced-sale proceeds first address outstanding debt and assigned reserve under the position rules. A zero contract price does not create a risk-free acquisition: token transfer behavior, debt settlement, competing transactions and state changes still matter.

What a read interface should show

  • Position and hub identity, challenge index, size, collateral decimals and stored price.
  • Challenge start, challenge period, current phase, source block and exact boundary comparisons.
  • Challenged amount, expiration, expired-purchase price and any postponed collateral return.
  • Unknown or stale state as unavailable—not as no challenge or zero price.
No challenger, bidder, keeper or postponed-return automation is provided. Participants must assess and execute their own transactions. Repayment is a separate path and can remain possible during a challenge or after expiry; see repayment and withdrawal.

label: Participants & vetoes
title: Qualified votes, separate clocks, no hidden administrator
intro: Understand time-weighted qualification, proposal vetoes and rate changes without conflating their windows.
html:
Time-weighted votes and helpers

An account's own votes are based on its pool-share balance and holding-time anchor. Qualification requires votes × 10,000 > 200 × totalVotes, equivalent to strictly more than 2%. Exactly 2% does not qualify. When total votes are zero, a zero-vote caller also fails; the comparison is deliberately not written as a permissive greater-than-or-equal check.

The helpers array must be sorted in strictly increasing address order, contain no duplicates or sender, and contain only accounts that directly or indirectly delegate to the caller. For a chain A → B → C, caller C must include both A and B to count both. It is the caller's responsibility to discover valid delegators; an invalid list can make the call revert.

Position veto: before start only

A new position has an initialization period of at least three days. A qualified caller can deny it only while now < start. At start, denial is too late. Initial cooldown equals start, and minting requires now > cooldown, so exactly start is neither a valid veto time nor a valid mint time.

Minter applications are a separate process

A new minter application uses the currency token's configured MIN_APPLICATION_PERIOD and a minimum application fee of 1,000 local units. That period is configured per deployment and must not be confused with the position's three-day minimum or the leadrate's seven-day delay. Minter denial remains possible through now == validityStart and is too late only when now > validityStart; minter status begins at now ≥ validityStart. Review the exact timestamp and state rather than assuming a common window.

Leadrate changes are proposed, then applied

A qualified caller can propose nextRatePPM, which sets nextChange = proposalTime + 7 days. The current rate does not change automatically at that timestamp. Anyone can call applyChange() once now ≥ nextChange; until that call, the old current rate continues to accrue. A later proposal overwrites the pending value and resets the delay. See savings and rate clocks.

Genesis is deployer-only and supply-gated

V2 genesis registers exactly five minters: Savings, PositionFactory, PositionRoller, MintingHub and the source bridge. Only the deployer can call initialize, and only while both currency-token supply and pool-share supply are zero. This is a genesis path, not an ongoing allocation or rate administrator.

V2 has no GuardianTimelock, guardian/admission administrator, owner-controlled pause, replacement timelock or allocation minter. Later public minter applications and qualified pool-share governance are separate from deployer genesis.

No certification is implied

Removing guardian controls does not by itself certify decentralization or regulatory compliance. No MiCA compliance, official affiliation or audit coverage is asserted. Participants must review the actual V2 source, deployment identity and unresolved production source-asset assumptions.

Read participation responsibilities

label: Reserves & equity
title: One currency. Several economic roles.
intro: Spendable currency, assigned minter reserves and pool-share equity are related, but they are not interchangeable.
html:
What the bootstrap establishes

On the test deployment path, six-decimal Test USDC is locked in each currency's own bridge, which mints 100 nominal local units. Investing those 100 local units into an empty Equity contract issues exactly 1,000 pool shares. The valuation factor is 3, so the post-investment price is 3 × equity ÷ totalShares = 0.3 local units per share. Before that investment, an empty system reports a price of 1; do not confuse the two states.

The test source has no real collateral value and deployer-gated test minting. The sequence tests contract accounting, not market backing or a production source-asset decision.

Later equity quotes are nonlinear

After the initial/low-capital branch, investment share issuance scales with the cubic root of the capital ratio, and redemption proceeds use a cubic relationship. In the nonlinear investment branch, a 0.3% fee factor (997 / 1000) reduces the investment used in the share calculation; redemption applies the same factor to the shares used in its proceeds calculation. A later share price is therefore not fixed at 0.3, and a simple linear pro-rata calculation is not an exact quote.

Use calculateShares and calculateProceeds at an identified block, and supply minimum expected shares or proceeds in a separately authorized transaction to limit adverse state changes. This integration reads and plans only; it does not simulate or execute those transactions.

The 100-unit floor and recapitalization

MINIMUM_EQUITY is 100 local units. An investment must leave equity at or above that floor. When capital before investment is below 100, or share supply is zero, issuance uses the fixed 1,000-share branch rather than the normal cubic-root branch. When equity is below 100, strictly qualified pool-share voters can also restructure the cap table by burning listed share balances.

These are recapitalization mechanics, not a recovery promise. New capital can absorb losses and alter ownership and dilution; the 100-unit threshold is an economic rule, not insured backing.

Holding duration and redemption

Redemption requires the owner's average share holding duration to be at least 90 days. Additional shares and transfers can change that weighted average. The redemption amount must leave more than one pool share in total supply: in raw 18-decimal units, redeemedShares + 1e18 < totalSupply. Redeeming everything or leaving exactly one share fails.

Reserve balances and current assigned reserve

The Equity contract holds local tokens for both tracked minter reserve and pool-share equity. Currency-token equity is the reserve balance minus tracked minter reserve, floored at zero. Fees and settlement outcomes change these balances. Severe losses can impair minter reserve, after which the original reserve percentage no longer determines current assigned reserve or repayment proceeds. See repayment arithmetic.

Equity is a separate risk participation

Pool shares are not currency tokens and do not represent DEX liquidity. Their value can rise or fall with the system. Savings interest is limited by available equity and is not a fixed claim on source assets or sovereign-bond income. Read savings and rate clocks or return to the mechanism overview.

label: System architecture
title: A framework of independent currency instances.
intro: Zoom out to the framework, then zoom into a single position and its read boundary.
html:
Framework level

The website, documentation, app, SDK and MCP share vocabulary and exact read/plan models across 11 currency codes. This does not merge token supply, debt, reserve accounting, pool shares, savings or bridge caps. Cross-currency aggregation would be a separate product and risk design, not an implicit feature of this frontend.

Currency and position level

A verified currency registry identifies Token, Equity, PositionFactory, PositionRoller, Savings, MintingHub, Bridge and source. Deployment constructor arguments, transactions and postconditions are evidence about deployment, not substitutes for current state. Within a currency, each position holds its own collateral while family capacity and reserve accounting follow the contract relationships.

Registry verification is a gate

Before calling state verified, an integration must check protocol generation, network and chain ID, deployed bytecode, constructor linkage and cross-contract addresses. It must not substitute legacy V1 addresses, generated fixtures or an artifact merely labeled with a schema version. No current V2 deployment registry is configured here, so live read reconciliation and production availability remain unclaimed.

Interface and integration level

The browser-safe SDK and MCP adapter provide read-only access to the same models. Humans and agents receive the same raw values, exact arithmetic, assumptions and source-block metadata. Registry import, RPC reads and local planning are separate from signer infrastructure.

Read health is part of architecture

Every read model needs chain and contract identity, block number, block timestamp and freshness status. Unconfigured, loading, empty, wrong-chain, missing-code, failed, unknown and stale states remain distinct. They never become zero balances, zero debts, zero rates, no challenge or available capacity by default.

Local drafts are not network state

Browser drafts stay on the app origin with no cloud synchronization. They can preserve assumptions and user-entered values, but cannot establish deployment, ownership, eligibility, authorization or confirmation. See agent workflows and source bridge architecture.

label: Borrowing costs
title: Quote gross debt, reserve, upfront fee and usable proceeds
intro: V2 borrowing cost is a time-based contract calculation, not a fixed 20%/1% teaching model.
html:
Start with the operation type

  • New proposal: pays an irrevocable OPENING_FEE of 1,000 local units (1000 × 1e18 raw), then any mint uses the upfront reserve/fee calculation below.
  • Clone accepted terms: does not pay the opening fee, but its mandatory initial mint still uses reserve and upfront fee arithmetic with the child's expiration.
  • Existing-position mint: has no new opening fee; reserve, fee, capacity, backing and eligibility still apply.

Annual interest has two components

annualInterestPPM = hub.rate.currentRatePPM + riskPremiumPPM. In V2, the hub's rate contract is the currency's Savings contract. The current leadrate is therefore the baseline for both savings ticks and position minting fees. The risk premium is immutable for the position family; the leadrate can change through the separate proposal and applyChange process.

The exact forward quote

quoteTime = max(blockTimestamp, start)
seconds = expirationForQuote − quoteTime
feePPM = min(1,000,000, floor(seconds × annualInterestPPM / 365 days))
usable = floor(gross × (1,000,000 − reserveContributionPPM − feePPM) / 1,000,000)

gross and usable are 18-decimal local amounts; rates are ppm and times are seconds. The fee calculation requires an expiration at or after quoteTime to avoid underflow, while actual minting separately requires now < expiration. Reserve plus fee must be at most 1,000,000 ppm or the allocation arithmetic is invalid and reverts. A positive usable amount generally requires their sum to be below 1,000,000 ppm and enough gross amount to survive integer rounding.

Use the correct expiration

calculateCurrentFee() always uses the position's own stored expiration. For an existing mint, that is the relevant quote. For a custom-expiration child, call parent.calculateFee(childExpiration); the parent's current-expiration getter is the wrong input. The eventual child mint uses the child expiration and the leadrate at execution.

Pre-opening quotes contain assumptions

Before a new position exists, a planner can only combine the current hub leadrate read with proposed risk premium, reserve and assumed block/start/expiration timestamps. It must label those assumptions and source block. Initialization and later rate changes can produce a different execution fee. This read/plan output is not transaction simulation, an allowance check by itself or a guaranteed executable quote.

The inverse is rounded up

To target usable proceeds, V2 computes the corresponding gross amount without the family limit:

usableTarget = 0 → gross = 0
otherwise gross = floor((usableTarget × 1,000,000 − 1)
                      / (1,000,000 − reserveContributionPPM − feePPM)) + 1

This is the rounded-up inverse, not a rounded-down division. Recompute the forward usable amount and check the denominator before using the result. In the illustrative figure, targeting 74,000 usable units returns 100,000 gross under the same assumptions.

A quote never proves mint eligibility

Separately verify owner-or-roller caller rights, challengedAmount == 0, not closed, now > cooldown, now < expiration, available family capacity and collateral backing. Original and clone family capacity differ in how unused original potential is reserved. availableForMinting() intentionally does not check challenge, closure or cooldown. Unknown or stale inputs make the plan unknown, not zero-cost or eligible.

Next: repay wallet currency against gross debt or review expiration and rolling.

label: Repayment & withdrawal
title: Repay debt first; check collateral withdrawal separately
intro: Wallet amount, gross debt reduction, assigned reserve and collateral release are four different quantities.
html:
The three repayment amounts

repay(amount) takes an 18-decimal local wallet amount excluding reserve. The currency contract calculates freedAmount, which is the gross reduction in position.minted. The difference freedAmount − amount is the currently assigned reserve moved into the position and included in the burn. The return value is the gross debt reduction, not the wallet debit.

When reserve coverage is unimpaired, the normal calculation is freed = floor(amount × 1,000,000 / (1,000,000 − reserveContributionPPM)). If the reserve token balance is below tracked minter reserve, V2 first reduces the effective reserve ppm proportionally:

adjustedReservePPM = floor(reserveContributionPPM × currentReserveBalance
                           / trackedMinterReserve)   // only when impaired
freedAmount = floor(amount × 1,000,000 / (1,000,000 − adjustedReservePPM))

This is why the initial reserve percentage is not a perpetual repayment ratio. Read the current reserve token balance, tracked minter reserve and position reserve contribution at the same block.

Full repayment needs a candidate and simulation

PositionRoller.findRepaymentAmount(position) performs a binary search using current reserve coverage and integer rounding. It can provide a full-repayment candidate; simply multiplying gross debt by one minus the original reserve ratio is not an exact general method. The candidate is state-dependent and must be checked with a simulation of the actual repayment before a separate signer acts. This integration does not perform that simulation.

If the calculated debt reduction exceeds minted, repayment reverts rather than silently clamping. At a 100% reserve contribution with unimpaired adjusted reserve, the freed-amount denominator is zero and the standard quote/candidate path reverts. Treat that edge as an explicit contract state—not zero debt, zero payment or a valid quote.

Debt-free is not closed

Reducing minted to zero does not set the position's closed flag. A debt-free position can potentially mint again if all other checks pass. Closure results from governance denial or from a collateral withdrawal that leaves less than the minimum collateral.

Withdrawal has separate restrictions

Collateral withdrawal requires the owner or recognized roller, no open challenge and now > cooldown. The post-withdrawal balance must still satisfy collateral backing. If the balance falls below minimumCollateral, the position is marked closed; exactly at the minimum does not close it. With positive debt, below-minimum collateral counts as zero for backing and therefore cannot pass. In practice, full withdrawal normally follows full repayment.

A closed position can still have collateral withdrawn subject to challenge, cooldown and backing checks. Closure blocks further minting but is not a blanket freeze on every function.

Repayment and withdrawal clocks differ

repay does not have the minting path's no-challenge, no-cooldown or before-expiration modifiers. Repayment can therefore remain possible during a challenge, during cooldown and after expiration, subject to token and state behavior. Do not block a repayment plan merely because withdrawal is unavailable; do not infer that repayment also unlocks collateral.

Management checklist

  1. Read gross minted, reserve contribution, current reserve balances and candidate wallet amount at one block.
  2. Read collateral balance, minimum, price, challengedAmount, cooldown, expiration, closure and caller/roller identity separately.
  3. Label failed or stale reads unknown and preserve the source block.
  4. Before any external execution, simulate the exact repay or withdraw call and reconcile the confirmed debt and balances afterward.

Continue with maturity and rolling or challenge restrictions.

label: Maturity & rolling
title: Expiration closes some paths, not every obligation
intro: Track start, cooldown and expiration independently; treat rolling as a new transaction with its own failure conditions.
html:
Start, cooldown and expiration

For a new position, start = deploymentTimestamp + initializationPeriod, with initialization of at least three days. Initial cooldown = start, and expiration = start + duration. A veto requires now < start; minting requires now > cooldown and now < expiration. Exactly at start, neither veto nor initial mint is available.

Raising a liquidation price imposes a three-day cooldown. Averting a challenge imposes one day, and a successful challenge imposes three days. These restrictions affect minting and withdrawal differently: repayment can remain available, while collateral withdrawal still requires no challenge and a timestamp strictly after cooldown.

At and after expiration

No mint or new challenge can begin at or after expiration. Existing challenges and settlement still matter, and collateral withdrawal remains blocked while a challenge is open. Repayment does not have the before-expiration modifier and can remain possible.

If there is no open challenge, the expired forced-sale path starts at 10× liquidation price at expiration, reaches 1× after one challenge period and reaches zero after two. It is distinct from an ordinary challenge auction. See the exact challenge and expired-sale boundaries.

What rolling actually does

The PositionRoller can atomically use a local-currency flash loan to repay a source position, withdraw source collateral, mint into a target position and repay the flash loan from the caller's resulting funds. Source and target must use the same collateral, the caller must own the source, both positions must be recognized, and both hubs must recognize the roller. Collateral allowances, target capacity, backing, fees, cooldowns, challenges and expiration still apply.

If the target is not already owned by the caller or its expiration differs from the requested expiration, the roller clones it. Otherwise it can use the existing target. Excess collateral or insufficient target minting can leave the caller needing additional local currency to repay the flash loan; review the exact amounts rather than assuming a self-funding roll.

Custom expiration needs full simulation

rollFully uses the target's existing expiration. rollFullyWithExpiration accepts another expiration, but its helper still derives a mint candidate with target.getMintAmount(repay), which uses the target's current-expiration fee getter. It does not substitute the custom expiration into that quote. Target fee, required collateral and available mint can therefore differ from the helper's estimate.

A custom-expiration roll requires simulation of the complete transaction and is not guaranteed by the view helpers. Check source repayment, withdrawal restrictions, clone constraints, child expiration, target capacity, target mint and final flash-loan repayment together. This read-only integration does not simulate, sign or execute a roll.

Maturity checklist

  1. Read source and target owners, hubs, roller, collateral, family terms and current block.
  2. Compare start, cooldown, expiration and challenge state with exact strict/non-strict boundaries.
  3. Calculate repayment using current reserve coverage and the correct target expiration for any new quote.
  4. Keep enough collateral and local currency allowances/funding for the chosen external execution path.
  5. After any separately authorized transaction, read both positions and all wallet balances again; do not infer success from a plan.
No automatic rolling, expiry keeper or challenger infrastructure is included. The project operator remains responsible for preparing and acting before deadlines.

label: Source bridges & credits
title: Normalize decimals, not exchange rates
intro: A same-chain source bridge locks source tokens and mints equal nominal local units under a local cap and horizon.
html:
Use method-specific units

The source token must have fixed decimals no greater than 18. The local token always uses 18 decimals, and decimalMultiplier = 10^(18 − sourceDecimals). mint and mintTo accept source raw units, transfer them from the caller and mint amount × decimalMultiplier local raw units to the target.

For six-decimal Test USDC, the multiplier is 1e12. Thus 100 × 1e6 source raw units produce 100 × 1e18 local raw units: 100 nominal source units to 100 nominal local units. The test token is valueless, so this fixture is neither fiat backing nor an FX rate.

Cap and horizon use different checks

minted and limit are both outstanding local 18-decimal raw amounts, not source raw amounts. A mint that brings minted exactly to limit is allowed; exceeding the cap reverts. Burning decreases minted by the actual rounded local amount burned.

The bridge horizon is deployment time plus 52 weeks. New minting reverts only when now > horizon, so minting is still accepted exactly at the horizon and stops afterward. Redemption methods do not have that horizon check and can continue after it, subject to source-token behavior and available bridge assets.

Burning rounds down to a whole source unit

burn, burnAndSend and burnAndCredit accept local 18-decimal raw amounts. The bridge computes sourceAmount = floor(localAmount / decimalMultiplier) and burns only sourceAmount × decimalMultiplier. Any local remainder stays unburned with the holder. If the input is smaller than one whole source raw unit, the rounded source and burned amounts are zero.

burn sends source tokens to the caller; burnAndSend sends them to the selected target. These are immediate transfers, unlike credits.

Credits require a later payout

burnAndCredit(target, localAmount) burns the rounded local amount from the caller and records source raw units in credits[target]. It does not transfer source tokens to the target at that point. Anyone can later call payoutCredit(target), which pays the entire outstanding credit and clears it. The bridge's balanceOf(account) read returns this source-denominated credit, not a local-token balance.

Credits can be useful when a recipient cannot immediately receive the source token. They do not remove issuer blacklist, pause, upgrade or transfer restrictions, and a recorded credit is not evidence that payout has occurred.

Source trust remains a launch gate

This is a same-chain lock/mint module, not a cross-chain messaging bridge and not backing for unrelated position issuance. Production requires a separately approved DogeOS source asset and reviewed per-currency caps. Issuer control, upgradeability, minting, pause, blacklist, decimals, ERC20 behavior, redemption and liquidity assumptions remain unresolved. No production source asset or live bridge registry is configured in this integration.

Read before planning

Read source and local token addresses, decimals, multiplier, local cap, local minted amount, horizon, source balance and account credit at an identified block. Preserve both raw-unit systems in any JSON plan. Unknown or stale cap/credit reads are unavailable, not zero. For the test genesis relationship to pool shares, see reserves and equity.

label: Savings & rate clocks
title: Savings has its own account clock and a governed leadrate
intro: Withdrawal delay, accrued interest, current rate and pending rate are separate reads for each currency.
html:
One per-currency leadrate, two protocol uses

Each currency's Savings contract contains its own Leadrate state, separate from other currencies and from equity share pricing. The minting hub reads that same current leadrate as the baseline for position borrowing fees. Savings and borrowing therefore share the current on-chain rate within one currency; they are not independent rate oracles.

Deposits and the weighted withdrawal delay

New savings are subject to an interest and withdrawal delay of up to 3 days. When an account already has savings, the contract combines the old account ticks and the new deposit using a weighted average. Adding funds can therefore change the delay for the whole account rather than creating an independent lock for every deposit. While the account's stored ticks are ahead of current ticks, interest calculation and withdrawal are both blocked.

Withdrawal reverts while the account remains locked. After unlocking, a partial withdrawal reduces saved balance; requesting at least the full available amount withdraws all and clears the account. Read the account and current ticks at an identified block instead of assuming exactly 72 hours for every top-up. New saving is disabled when the current rate is zero, or when a pending zero rate is due within the three-day interest-delay window.

Interest accrual and the equity cap

The account's saved balance and tick delta determine linear interest: floor((ticks − account.ticks) × saved / 1,000,000 / 365 days). The result is capped by the currency system's available equity at calculation time. If equity is zero, newly calculated interest is zero. This cap means the nominal leadrate is not a guaranteed payment rate.

accruedInterest is a view, not a transfer. refreshBalance collects accrued interest into the saved balance, allowing later accrual on the increased balance; it does not withdraw to the wallet. Savings interest is not sovereign-bond income, source-stablecoin yield or an equity-share return.

Pending and current rates are not interchangeable

A strictly qualified pool-share caller proposes nextRatePPM, setting nextChange seven days after the proposal. The proposal does not change currentRatePPM. At or after nextChange, an explicit applyChange() call is required. Until that transaction, ticks continue at the old current rate; applying late does not retroactively activate the new rate at the proposal deadline.

A new proposal overwrites the pending rate and resets the seven-day delay. Proposing the existing current rate can cancel a pending change. Interfaces must show current and pending values, their source block and whether the change is ready but unapplied.

Dated initial configuration—not current rates

The deployment snapshot was retrieved on 2026-10-24 and is marked implementation-reviewed / production-refresh-required. It combines normalized one-year reference-yield evidence with a 1.50-percentage-point (15,000 ppm) spread, then configures only the initial on-chain leadrate. It does not fetch live rates. The following are dated inputs in ppm, with percent-per-year equivalents for readability, not current return promises:

  • USD: 59,400 ppm (5.94%); observation 2026-10-23.
  • EUR: 44,113 ppm (4.4113%); observation 2026-10-22, using the ECB euro-area AAA curve with continuous-rate normalization.
  • JPY: 31,600 ppm (3.16%); observation 2026-10-22.
  • GBP: 60,132 ppm (6.0132%); observation 2026-10-22, with continuous-rate normalization.
  • AUD: 64,500 ppm (6.45%); observation 2026-10-23. Caveat: based on a secondary 52-week-bill source; exact primary one-year benchmark approval is still pending.
  • CNY: 26,800 ppm (2.68%); observation 2026-10-23.
  • BRL: 143,569 ppm (14.3569%); observation 2026-10-23, using the stated annual curve convention.
  • PKR: 139,999 ppm (13.9999%); observation 2026-10-14, using an auction cutoff rather than weighted-average yield.
  • BDT: 102,400 ppm (10.24%); observation 2026-10-18, published 2026-10-19, using the auction cutoff.
  • INR: 79,891 ppm (7.9891%); observation 2026-10-14. Caveat: uses the last successful auction because the newer 2026-10-21 auction accepted NIL; refresh and reassess staleness before any deployment.
  • NGN: 204,061 ppm (20.4061%); observation 2026-10-14. Caveat: derived from a 15.9% marginal discount rate using the documented discount-to-investment-yield formula, not a directly published official true yield; that basis requires validation or formal approval.

Production deployment requires a refreshed and reviewed complete snapshot. If a verified registry is later configured, use currentRatePPM and pending state from the selected block, not this list. No live V2 registry is configured now.

Keep savings, equity and borrowing distinct

Saved currency is not a pool share, and pool shares do not have the savings withdrawal clock. Equity has separate nonlinear quotes, a 90-day average holding rule and a more-than-one-share redemption constraint. Borrowing adds the position risk premium and time-to-expiration fee calculation to the same current baseline leadrate. Continue to equity mechanics or borrowing costs.
